title: Arbitrary privileged session minting through exported createSession action
description: An unauthenticated caller can directly invoke the exported Server Action with attacker-selected session fields. The action signs and sets a 30-day auth_session cookie, allowing the caller to choose the admin role.
root_cause: createSession in src/actions/auth.ts does not restrict direct callers or derive session claims server-side, allowing arbitrary privileged session issuance.
intended_behavior: Only completed authentication and authorization flows should create a session using server-derived claims.

trace.description: A Server Action export accepts caller-provided SessionData.
The caller-provided data is forwarded unchanged to the session writer.
A signed auth_session cookie is written with the supplied role and identity claims.

payloads: A direct Server Action request with SessionData containing role admin and a chosen identity.
instructions: Invoke the exported action directly through the Server Action protocol.
Use the cookie on protected routes.
execution.expected_result: The caller receives an authenticated session carrying attacker-chosen authorization claims.

remediation.strategy: Make session issuance private and derive every claim only after a server-side authentication flow succeeds.

likelihood.reason: The action is remotely dispatchable without authentication.

impact.reason: An attacker can mint an admin session.

confidence.reason: Source trace and the Next Server Action manifest confirm remote exposure and cookie issuance.

title: Account takeover through loginWithVerifiedContact
description: The public Server Action signs in any supplied registered contact without password, OTP, Turnstile, or a prior server-side challenge.
root_cause: loginWithVerifiedContact in src/actions/auth.ts does not verify control of the supplied contact before creating a session, allowing account takeover.
intended_behavior: A member session should be created only after password or contact-OTP verification.

trace.description: The Server Action accepts an arbitrary contact string.
The contact is used to resolve the registered member or household without proof of possession.
The action creates a signed session for the resolved account.

conditions.description: The target has a known live registered email address or phone number.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated caller who knows a target contact.
payloads: The target's normalized registered email address or phone number.
instructions: Invoke the Server Action directly with the target contact.
execution.expected_result: The caller is authenticated as the target member or household head.

remediation.strategy: Remove this unauthenticated action or require an already verified server-side OTP challenge bound to the contact.

likelihood.reason: Registered contacts are commonly discoverable or known.

impact.reason: The attacker gains target account capabilities.

confidence.reason: The action lacks all proof-of-control checks before session creation.

title: Stored XSS through unvalidated business social links
description: Business social links are stored without URL validation and rendered as raw public href values. A javascript URL executes when a visitor clicks it.
root_cause: createBusinessProfile in src/actions/business.ts does not validate socialLinks before persistence, allowing executable URL schemes to reach public href rendering.
intended_behavior: Business profiles should publish only safe external social-network URLs.

trace.description: Social links are JSON-persisted without scheme validation.
A stored social link is rendered directly into an href attribute.

conditions.description: The attacker can create or edit a business profile that is published.
A public visitor clicks the malicious social link.

instructions: Store the malicious social URL in a business profile.
Have the profile approved or use a live profile.
Induce a visitor to click the rendered social icon.
execution.expected_result: JavaScript executes in the visitor's application-origin browser context.

remediation.strategy: Allow only canonical HTTPS URLs for approved social hosts at write time and omit non-HTTPS links at render time.

likelihood.reason: Any approved business owner can store the payload.

impact.reason: Victim-session JavaScript execution can perform authenticated actions.

confidence.reason: The storage and public raw-href trace is directly present in source.
